THIS MOTOR ACCIDENT CLAIMS APPEAL HAVING COME UP FOR ADMISSION ON 06.01.2026, ALONG WITH MACA.537/2022, THE COURT ON THE SAME DAY DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 4 MACA Nos.537 and 584 of 2022 2026:KER:653  JUDGMENT [MACA Nos.537,584 of 2022]

These two appeals are instituted by the insurance company as well as the legal heirs of one Maheen, aged 32 years, challenging the award dated 08.10.2021 in O.P.(MV)
No.138 of 2016 of the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Punalur.

2. Heard Sri. Jacob Mathew, the learned Standing Counsel for the Insurance Company, as well as Sri. Anil K. Muhammed, the learned counsel for the claimants.
3. The deceased was stated to be employed in Riyadh as a Showroom in-charge, earning a monthly salary of Saudi Riyal 3,550.
While he was on leave in India from April 2015, he met with an accident on 06.06.2015 and succumbed to the injuries.
The vehicle concerned was owned by one Amina, who was none other than the widow of the deceased.
The legal heirs of the deceased Mahin, including Amina, instituted the claim petition before the Tribunal.
In the claim petition, Amina--the owner of the vehicle--was also impleaded as the first respondent.

4. The Tribunal refused to act upon Exhibits A6 and A7, documents produced by the claimants in support of the monthly MACA Nos.537 and 584 of 2022 2026:KER:653 income and fixed the notional income at Rs.10,000/- per month.

5. The Insurance Company instituted M.A.C.A. No.537 of 2022, essentially contending that the Tribunal failed to notice that Amina, the insured owner and widow of the deceased, could not be Abdul Majeed vs Amina on 6 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/32655276/
3 compensated.
The legal heirs of the deceased instituted M.A.C.A. No.584 of 2022, seeking enhancement of compensation, essentially with reference to the fixation of the notional income, as noticed earlier.
6. As regards M.A.C.A. No.537 of 2022, there is no dispute that Amina, the insured, was impleaded in the claim petition and was one of the legal heirs of the deceased.
The Insurance Company had specifically pointed out that Amina, being the registered owner as well as the insured of the vehicle in question, could not claim compensation.
Though this contention was recorded by the Tribunal, it was not specifically discussed or answered.
7. I have considered the submissions made with reference to the afore-stated contention.
This Court notices that the MACA Nos.537 and 584 of 2022 2026:KER:653 liability, if any, would be on the driver of the offending vehicle as well as the insured, Amina.
When that be so, Amina cannot independently institute a claim petition seeking compensation, even if the deceased was her husband.
To that extent, the appeal instituted by the Insurance Company is allowed, and it is held that Amina would not be entitled to compensation.

However, this Court in Oriental Insurance Co.
Ltd., Ekm v. Rajasree V.P. [2025 KHC OnLine 960], wherein the dependant daughter was the insured owner of the vehicle involved in the death of the father, had held that the daughter would be entitled for compensation under the head of 'consortium'.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, Amina would be entitled to compensation under the head 'consortium', which will be considered separately in the connected appeal.

8. With reference to the appeal instituted by the claimants --M.A.C.A. No.584 of 2022, this Court notes that they relied upon Exhibits A6 and A7 to contend that the deceased was earning a monthly income of Saudi Riyal 3,550.

The Tribunal, however,
refused to accept the same, with reference to the principles laid down in Valsamma v. Binue Jose (2014 (1) MACA Nos.537 and 584 of 2022 2026:KER:653 KLT 10).

entities.text: Valsamma v. Binue Jose (2014 (1) MACA Nos.537 and 584 of 2022 2026:KER:653 KLT 10)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the present case, the certificate at Exhibit A7 is attested by the Embassy of India, Riyadh.
When that be so, the said documents could be acted upon, with reference to the provisions of the Diplomatic and Consular Officers (Oaths and Fees) Act,1948.

entities.text: Diplomatic and Consular Officers (Oaths and Fees) Act,1948.
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Therefore, I am of the opinion that the Tribunal erred in discarding the employment certificate at Exhibit A7 relied upon by the claimants.
9. At the same time, the question arises as to whether the entire amount shown in the certificate could be accepted as the monthly income of the deceased.
The fact that the deceased was working and residing in Riyadh means that at least 50% of the income should be allocated for his personal needs, with the balance considered as the notional income.
When that be so, I am of the opinion that the notional income of the deceased could be fixed at Rs. 31,000/- per month.
To that extent, the award of the Tribunal requires modification, and accordingly, I do so.
10. As regards the compensation under the head of 'consortium', Amina would be entitled for an amount of Rs.40,000/- as already discussed above.

In the result, both appeals are partly allowed, modifying the impugned award, entitling the appellant/claimants 1,2, and 4 in the M.A.C.A No.584 of 2022 to get an additional amount of Rs.35,39,200/- (Rupees Thirty Five Lakhs Thirty Nine Thousand and Two Hundred only), and the 3rd appellant/claimant in the same appeal to get only an amount of Rs.40,000/- (Rupees MACA Nos.537 and 584 of 2022 2026:KER:653 Forty Thousand only) along with the amounts already awarded by the Tribunal, to be paid by the Insurance Company.
Needless to say, all other findings and directions of the Tribunal in the impugned award, including the rate of interest, will remain unaltered.
